[Sat 2026-05-02 01:01 EDT] Write a sermon manuscript for Week 4 of the "Defined - Who God Says You Are" series.

**Sermon Title:** "God Says I Am More Than a Conqueror"
**Date:** May 3, 2026
**Passage:** Romans 8:28-39 (primary), Philippians 3:20 (supporting)
**Runtime Target:** 35-40 minutes

---

## VOICE & STYLE GUIDANCE

Write in the voice of a warm, authoritative, modern pastoral communicator — someone who is direct, relatable, theologically grounded, and practical. Think: warm big brother who also happens to be the pastor. Conversational but not casual. Theologically precise but not academic. Real illustrations, real stories, real application.

---

## SERMON OUTLINE:

### INTRODUCTION (hook):
"There's a word that the world uses a lot that actually describes what God does in you — and most Christians have never heard it this way."

Most people think identity is declared — God says who you are, you believe it, done. But Paul doesn't just declare identity in Romans 8 — he describes something being produced in you.

The word is hyper-nikomen — "more than conquerors." That's not a label. That's a transformation.

**The question this week: "Is that identity actually being produced in your life?"**

[PASTOR CHRIS WILL INSERT HIS PERSONAL STORY HERE — a time when he tried to manufacture something in his own strength and it backfired, then a moment when he stopped and let God work.]

---

### POINT 1: YOU BECOME THE VICTOR
**Romans 8:28**
**Identity Marker:** You are not a victim of your circumstances — you are the inheritor of God's purpose.

**The Truth:** When you trust that God works all things together for good, you stop waiting for victory and start inheriting it. You're not hoping to win — you already have it.

**Observation:** People treat their circumstances as the evidence of God's favor instead of God's presence as the evidence. They're waiting to see victory before they inherit it — when the promise says the inheriting happens now, by faith.

**Application:** When difficulty hits — a hard email, a bad diagnosis, a broken relationship — instead of spiraling into "How am I going to fix this?" — say: "God is working this for my good."

**Quotable Line:** "God doesn't promise to give you a good story. He promises to write a good ending into yours."

**Illustration:** Post-it Notes — Spencer Silver accidentally created a weak adhesive that 3M couldn't use for 5 years. Art Fry then used it for a hymn bookmark that wouldn't fall out — and it became one of 3M's most profitable products. The "flaw" became the feature. Your setbacks aren't wasted — God's redesigning around them.

**Next Steps:**
1. Each time a difficult situation arises this week, say out loud: "God is working this for my good."
2. Identify one circumstance you've been complaining about and write down how God might use it.
3. Stop one negative thought about your situation and replace it with the truth of Romans 8:28.

---

### POINT 2: YOU BECOME A WORSHIPPER
**Romans 8:31-32**
**Identity Marker:** You are not a Sunday singer — you are a 7-day-a-week worshiper.

**The Truth:** When you truly believe God gave His Son for you, worship stops being a Sunday performance and starts being a lifestyle. Your whole life becomes the song.

**Observation:** Worship has become an event instead of a posture. People check the box on Sunday and call it done — when the New Testament call is to offer your whole life as worship (Romans 12:1).

**Application:** Stop asking "Did I go to church?" and start asking "Did I worship?" Treat everything as worship — how you drive, how you speak to your kids, how you handle the difficult client.

**Quotable Line:** "The God who didn't spare His own Son will not hold back anything else either."

**Illustration:** Rites of Passage — Sociologists have studied how rituals actually transform identity. In cultures around the world, coming-of-age rituals don't just symbolize a transition — they produce it. The ritual creates the new identity. Christians have forgotten this. We treat worship as a symbol of faith rather than a mechanism of transformation. Every time you show up, every time you offer your Monday as worship, you're not just expressing who you are — you're forming who you are.

**Next Steps:**
1. Each morning this week, before checking your phone, say: "Lord, today is Yours — I'm worshipping You in how I work, speak, and love."
2. Choose one mundane task (driving, cooking, doing dishes) and intentionally do it as an act of worship this week.
3. This Sunday, after the service ends, ask one person: "How was your worship this week?" — and share how you worshipped in an ordinary moment.

---

### POINT 3: YOU BECOME ABLE
**Romans 8:34**
**Identity Marker:** You are not self-sufficient — you are Spirit-empowered.

**The Truth:** When you know Christ is actively interceding for you at this very moment, weakness stops being a liability. You're not capable in yourself — you're enabled by grace.

**Observation:** People treat grace as a backup plan when their strength runs out — when grace is supposed to be the primary source. They live as functional deists: "I do my best, and God helps where I'm lacking."

**Application:** Instead of white-knuckling in your own strength, start the day with: "I can't do this — but You can through me." When you hit a wall, instead of pushing harder, say "Lord, I need You in this."

**Quotable Line:** "You're not fighting alone. The one who defeated death is speaking up for you."

**Illustration:** John Wimber — founder of the Vineyard movement, used to say: "I have no confidence in my abilities for ministry. I have total confidence in the Holy Spirit." He wasn't being falsely humble — he was being theologically precise. He'd walk into a pastoral counseling situation knowing he wasn't enough, and say to the person: "Let's ask Someone who knows what they're doing." Ministry didn't flow from Wimber's sufficiency — it flowed through his insufficiency, by design.

**Next Steps:**
1. The next time you feel overwhelmed, stop and pray: "I am not enough for this. I need You." — before you do anything else.
2. Identify one area where you've been white-knuckling (a relationship, a habit, a responsibility) and confess: "I'm insufficient here, Lord. Work through me."
3. End each day this week by asking: "Where did I operate in my own strength today instead of depending on You?" — and name it specifically.

---

### POINT 4: YOU BECOME COURAGEOUS
**Romans 8:37**
**Identity Marker:** You are not afraid of the outcome — you are more than enough in Christ.

**The Truth:** "More than a conqueror" isn't just a title — it's a disposition that gets produced in you when you know the ending is secured. Courage isn't manufactured. It's grown.

**Observation:** People treat courage as a feeling they have to generate — when the biblical picture is the opposite. Courage is the overflow of knowing the ending. You don't conjure it; you receive it because you're secure in the Victor.

**Application:** When fear shows up — a hard conversation, a risky decision, a scary diagnosis — instead of asking "Do I have enough courage to do this?" ask "Am I trusting the One who already won?"

**Quotable Line:** "You don't just survive hard times. You come out of them with more of Christ than you went in with."

**Illustration:** Sold Out Concert Ticket — You have a ticket to a concert that's already sold out. Scalpers are offering 10x the price. But you don't have a ticket because you bought one — you have one because someone gave it to you. And it's guaranteed. You walk in without anxiety. That's what it's like to walk into hard conversations, difficult seasons, scary futures — not because you're brave enough, but because your ticket is already punched.

**Next Steps:**
1. The next time fear shows up, pause and say: "I am not called to be fearless. I am called to be faithful — and the outcome is already decided."

1 2 3 4 5 6 God Says I Am His Child — Week 1 7 15 16 17

God Says I Am His Child

18
19 Series: Defined — Who God Says You Are | Week 1 | April 12, 2026
20 Romans 8:1–17 | ReImage Church — Pastor Chris 21
22

Have you ever had someone try to give you something — a real gift, no strings — and you just couldn't take it?

23

Like, somebody at a restaurant says, "Hey, I got your meal." And before they even finish the sentence, you're reaching for your wallet. "No, no, no — let me at least get the tip." And they're like, "I said I got it." And you're like, "You sure? I can Venmo you." They are literally handing you a gift and you are negotiating your way into paying for it.

24

Come on. We all do this.

25

And here's the thing — we don't just do it at restaurants. We do it with God.

26

God says, "You're mine. You're in. You're my child." And we say, "Okay, but let me earn it first. Let me prove I'm worth it. Let me pray enough and read my Bible enough and serve enough and be good enough — and then maybe I'll believe it."

27

I want to be honest with you this morning. I've been a Christian for a long time. My dad was a pastor. I grew up in the church. I've been in ministry for decades. And there are still weeks — real weeks, recent weeks — where I wake up and the first thought in my head is, "Is God pleased with me today?" And that question sits on my chest like a weight. I know better. I know the theology. I can teach it. I've preached it to you. But knowing it and living in it are two different things.

28

How many of you have had that thought? Come on, don't be shy. I've had it this week.

29

That voice — the one that says you have to keep earning it, keep proving it, keep performing — that's what I call the orphan voice. And if you've heard it, this message is for you.

30

Because here's what God wants you to know today. You're not an orphan trying to earn a home. You're a child who's already home.

31

This is Week 1 of a new series called "Defined" — four weeks about who God says you are. Not who you think you are. Not who the world says you are. Who God says you are. And it starts here: you are His child.

32

Let me pray for us, and then we'll get into the text.

33

Father, we thank you that you've called us your children. Open our eyes to see who you say we are. Remove the lies we've believed about ourselves and replace them with your truth. We want to hear from you today. In Jesus' name, amen.

34

[FULL READING OF ROMANS 8:1–17 — INSERT HERE]

35

All right. I want to start with something that changed everything for me when I finally understood it. Because for a long time, I had the gospel partly right and partly sideways. And the part I had sideways was costing me more than I realized.

36

For years I thought forgiveness was the headline. The main event. I thought the gospel was basically: God forgives your sins, and if you hold it together, you get to go to heaven. And that is true — but it's not the whole truth. It's not even the best part.

37

Because here's what happens when forgiveness is your primary understanding of the Christian life. You wake up every day trying not to sin. You try to pray enough. You try to read your Bible enough. ...

100

The orphan asks, "Am I enough?" The child says, "My Father is."

101

Remember what I said at the beginning about the restaurant — somebody trying to pay you back for a free meal? Let me escalate that.

102

Imagine someone comes to you and says, "I want to give you a million dollars. No strings. It's yours. It's a gift."

103

And you take it. And it's amazing. But then — the next morning — you show up at their house. And you start cleaning. You're mopping their floors. Mowing their lawn. Washing their car. And they come outside and look at you like, "What are you doing?"

104

"Well, I just want to earn it. I want to prove I deserve it."

105

And they're looking at you like — "I gave you a million dollars so you'd never have to clean a house again. Not mine. Not yours. Not anybody's. Why are you trying to pay me back for something I gave you for free?"

106

That's us with God. He gives us everything — adoption, inheritance, the Holy Spirit, eternal life — and we keep showing up to clean the house. We keep trying to pay back a gift. And God is saying, "You're my child. Come inside. Sit down. You're home. Stop trying to pay for what's already yours."

107

You can't earn what was already given. That's what makes it grace.

108

So which voice are you living under?

109

Are you living under the orphan voice — always performing, always proving, always wondering if you've done enough? Or are you living under the Spirit's voice — the one that says no condemnation, you belong, you're in, you're mine?

110

When do you feel like you have to prove yourself to God? Is it when you mess up? When you skip your quiet time? When that shame starts creeping in? When you compare yourself to someone who seems like they've got it way more together than you do? Is it Sunday morning when you walk in here wondering if anyone can tell you didn't read your Bible all week?

111

That's the orphan voice. And it's lying to you. The Spirit is saying something different. "There is therefore now no condemnation." "The Spirit Himself bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God." The orphan voice says "prove it." The Spirit says "it's already proven."

112

You've got to learn to fight it. Not with more performance — with truth.

113

A couple things to sit with this week. You know the rhythm — starting points, not assignments. Listen for what God is actually saying.

114

Pay attention to when the orphan voice shows up. Just notice it. When does the anxiety hit? When do you feel like God is disappointed? Don't try to fix it yet — just name it. "That's the orphan voice." You can't fight what you can't see. Sometimes just naming it takes away half its power.

115

And write down three truths about who you are in Christ. "I am loved. I am chosen. I am His child. I belong. I am not condemned." Put them where the orphan voice is loudest — your mirror, your lock screen, your dashboard. When it talks, replace it with the truth. Out loud if you have to.

116

Or maybe God is asking you to sit with the older brother's story and ask yourself: "Where am I keeping score?" Listen. He knows what you need.

117

[TRANSITION]

118

Now I know where some of you are going. "Okay, Pastor Chris. If I'm already adopted. If I don't have to earn it. If the verdict is in — then what do I do? Do I just coast? Is it all grace and no obedience?"

119

No. And this is the part that changes how you actually live.

120

When you know whose you are, you know who you are. And that changes everything about how you live.

121

Here's what most of us have been doing. We've been trying to change our behavior so we can earn an identity. Pray more so God loves me more. Serve more so I feel like I belong. Read my Bible more so I can call myself a real Christian. We're working from the outside in. Behavior...
